functional_dependency.statement: Glycine supplies a co-substrate for AGAT-dependent guanidinoacetate formation, followed by GAMT-dependent creatine production.

dietary_supply.statement: Canonical Glycine composition records establish dietary amino-acid provision. Endogenous synthesis and homeostasis also contribute; dietary supply is not a claim of current deficiency or benefit above adequacy.

conversion_pathway.process: Human AGAT transfers the amidino group of arginine to glycine, yielding guanidinoacetate and ornithine.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Both co-substrates are required; this is not a fixed dietary yield or an assertion that extra intake is rate-limiting.

evidence.statement: UniProt P50440 entry version 227, Rhea 13201; human renal GAA production independently measured.

conversion_pathway.process: GAMT methylates guanidinoacetate using S-adenosylmethionine to form creatine.
dependencies: Interorgan exchange and receiving-tissue creatine transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity does not prove dietary precursor limitation or cerebral delivery; SAM participation creates no independent methionine admission.

assessment.assessment_limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing canonical amino-acid food composition is reused; no food is relabelled as containing GAA or extra creatine, and no dose equivalence is inferred.

assessment.operation: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

functional_dependency.statement: Dietary methionine supplies SAM through MAT-dependent activation, sustaining methyl-donor capacity for GAMT methylation of guanidinoacetate.

dietary_supply.statement: Canonical methionine food composition provides the same amino acid used by MAT; no food-dose equivalence to experimental diets is inferred.

conversion_pathway.process: MAT1A/MAT2A catalyse ATP-dependent methionine adenosylation to form SAM.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity establishes capacity, not a universal limiting intake or greater flux from additional intake.

evidence.statement: Human MAT crystallography and curated Rhea 21080; P31153 v237 and Q00266 v233.

assessment.assessment_limitations: Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. Neonatal-piglet isotope incorporation does not establish an adult intake target, cerebral delivery or benefit above adequacy. Methyl allocation, SAH inhibition, transport and other substrate availability constrain the route; no shared KC admission follows.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Reused existing methionine composition and preparation records; no SAM content or food efficacy edge inferred.

assessment.operation: Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.
assessment.assessment_limitations: Uncontrolled sequential exposure: C8/C10 mixture (n=11) then 95% tricaprylin (n=6), 30 g/day for one month each. No claim of isolated C8 superiority, cognitive efficacy, healthy-person requirement or ordinary coconut-oil equivalence. PET uptake/metabolism is not a direct cellular ATP assay; no food-effective dose or fixed conversion yield is inferred.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Inspected MCT Oil’s analytical product-specific triglyceride relationship and Coconut Oil’s explicit distinction between fatty-acid composition and individual triglycerides. Reuse only supported structured or independently researched material edges, retain formulation qualifiers and missing quantities; do not create a coconut-oil trioctanoin edge from C8 fatty-acid content.

functional_dependency.statement: Defined dietary caprylic triglyceride can supply hepatic ketone production and cerebral ketone-fuel availability for this ketone-utilisation operation.

dietary_supply.statement: The primary experiment used an orally administered tricaprylin-rich preparation. The MCT Oil record has a product/preparation-dependent caprylic-triglyceride relationship; fatty-acid content alone is not proof of trioctanoin content.

conversion_pathway.process: Digestive lipolysis releases C8 fatty acid from trioctanoin; the absorbed fatty acid is represented as octanoate at physiological pH.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition.

evidence.statement: Human triglyceride-lipase reaction provenance and the defined oral tricaprylin exposure; retrieved 26 October 2026.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.

assessment.operation: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.
assessment.assessment_limitations: Culture conditions and community composition constrain production. Human inulin tracer estimates depend on assumed systemic availability; the human chicory-inulin trial did not significantly increase faecal butyrate. No fixed food yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Inspected canonical inulin and onion records and the existing food-research ledger. No structured long-chain-specific food edge currently exists; mixed-fructan presence is insufficient to invent one. Dietary ingredient supply is established by oral human studies; exact food chain-length coverage remains an explicit ontology gap.

functional_dependency.statement: Inulin supplies fermentable carbohydrate for SCFA-producing microbial capacity; product distribution depends on community and culture or host conditions.

dietary_supply.statement: Defined oral inulin exposures are documented in human studies, including 15 g with breakfast in PMID 26516911. A formulated inulin ingredient is not interchangeable with every fructan food or oligofructose-enriched blend.

assessment.operation: Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.
assessment.assessment_limitations: Donor cultures do not establish a predictable whole-food conversion yield, mitochondrial effect or clinical benefit. Human apple-extract evidence involves mixed monomeric catechins, not isolated epicatechin efficacy. Do not generalise to EGCG or all procyanidins.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured composition and provisional food research for this exact canonical input were inspected. Reuse these source/form-qualified foods; do not infer an effective food dose or invent additional relationships.

functional_dependency.statement: Epicatechin supplies a defined microbial substrate for phenolic ring-fission and valerolactone-generation capacity.

dietary_supply.statement: Existing cocoa and dark-chocolate composition relationships document epicatechin presence without a verified concentration. Processing and matrix differences remain; these foods are substrate sources, not proven mitochondrial interventions.

assessment.operation: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.
assessment.assessment_limitations: Preparation-, dose- and population-specific. The positive study used 30 g/day for four weeks in ten healthy participants; this is not an effective whole-food dose. Preserve the later 40 g/day type-2-diabetes null. SCFA mediation and universal benefit are unestablished; no brain or ADHD inference.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured composition and provisional food research for this exact canonical input were inspected. Reuse these source/form-qualified foods; do not infer an effective food dose or invent additional relationships.

mechanism_engagement.statement: Defined oral resistant-starch supplementation modulated clamp-measured insulin sensitivity and post-meal forearm glucose clearance in a small human study.

dietary_exposure.statement: The dietary ingredient was administered orally and the same substrate class has form-dependent food-source records. Neither green-banana content nor cooling a food establishes equivalence to the tested resistant-starch supplement.
